history.dynasty: Legendary (Mahabharata-era); present structure attributed to Parmar kings; current form 18th century
history.period: Legendary antiquity; present structure 18th century (one source says 16th century AD - conflict, verify)
history.summary: The famous Parmat Shiva temple of Kanpur, on the banks of the Ganga at Parmat Ghat (Civil Lines). Legend links the site to Mahabharata-era Karna, who worshipped Shiva here. A cow named Anandi is said to have poured her milk daily on a mound; villagers dug the spot and found a self-manifested (Swayambhu) north-facing Shivling whose base could not be found, so they built the temple around it and named it after the cow. The present structure is attributed to Parmar kings and is said to date to the 18th century, with multiple renovations since (velpu.com says 16th century AD - conflict, verify). Features: hundreds of bells, a rare 12-window main gate, a silver pitcher on the ceiling from which Gangajal drips constantly onto the Shivling, and shrines to Ganesha, Annapurna, Kartik, Kaal Bhairav, Kali and Parvati within the complex. Identity confirmed - this is the famous Anandeshwar Temple of Kanpur.

name: Anandeshwar Temple (Parmat)
town_description: Parmat (Permat) is an old locality of Kanpur in the Civil Lines area, on the bank of the river Ganga at Parmat Ghat. The temple stands on several acres of land on the riverbank, with a spacious courtyard and subsidiary shrines around the main sanctum; the evening Ganga aarti at the ghat is an added attraction.

travel.airport: Kanpur Airport (Chakeri) is the nearest airport (per indiano.travel; verify distance).
travel.railway: Kanpur Central railway station is the nearest major railhead; about 20 minutes by cab to Parmat.
travel.road: On Parmat Road, Civil Lines, Kanpur 208001; well connected by road within the city.

visitor_information.best_time: November to February (winter); Maha Shivaratri and Shravan month are peak pilgrimage times.
